cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: Partition-level structural diagnostics provide triage evidence on internal subdivision and boundary proximity. All four candidate sets show screen_candidate_k=1 with large leading eigengaps (0.600-0.975) located at the single-cluster resolution, so the screening calculation does not show a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal for any set; this is absence of a detected subdivision signal, not evidence against independence from neighboring candidates. Within-set affinities range from 0.325 to 0.684, with the smaller sets (K6_C0005, K6_C0006) showing higher internal affinity than the two 36-member sets. Nearest-pair between-set affinities (0.079-0.124) are uniformly lower than within-set affinities, indicating the current boundaries are relatively well separated in the consensus geometry; the closest boundary is K6_C0002_M_K6_C0003 vs K6_C0005. These are partition-scope observations and do not establish biological meaning or clinical validity, nor do they prescribe retention, split, or merge.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: No prior reports were supplied for this round; this report is the sole structural evidence available. The partition-level screen does not provide feasible k>=2 solutions, so internal-subdivision evidence for any specific set is limited to the screening resolution.
